title: reliquary machine state
description: Synchronized companion to the instance model (instance-model.md), which remains normative. Describes machine.json — the per-machine state document reliquary writes under cache/machines/<id>/. reliquary authors this file (canonical strict JSON, no comments); the schema documents the recorded-output contract for consumers reading it out-of-band. Schema validity never implies a live, consistent machine: identity verification, lifecycle reconciliation, media re-verification, and the blueprint-digest/blueprint-source selection rules live in the instance model only. Only the identity core (id, blueprint, created, phase, generation) is required, because a machine caught mid-create carries just that transitional subset; a fully materialized (ready/running) machine additionally carries the resolved fields and drives below. While running, the live VM identity is folded into this file as the 'vm' section (written atomically with phase, so a stopped machine never carries a stale identity); it is absent when not running, and its endpoint is shaped by the backend adapter that recorded it. No $schema field is written pre-1.0.

id.description: The machine id, <blueprint>-<n>: the blueprint name (identity) and the lowest-free non-negative number at create time.

blueprint.description: The blueprint's identity name (its declared name, else its file stem) — the id's stem and the name-selection key.

created.description: Creation timestamp, UTC ISO 8601 to the second (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ).

phase.description: Lifecycle phase. The three transitional phases (creating/stopping/destroying) mark an operation in flight, reconciled at the next op.

generation.description: Operation generation: a monotonic counter bumped once per mutating operation, so an interrupted operation is detectable by phase and generation.

backend-id.description: The stable per-machine backend identity (reliquary-<id>), regenerated into the backend at each start.

blueprint-digest.description: sha256:<hex> over the resolved blueprint snapshot (cache paths excluded), so two machines of one blueprint share it and apply/start can detect blueprint drift.

blueprint-source.description: Absolute path of the blueprint file this machine resolved from, recorded for --blueprint selection scoping. Absent when the machine was created without a source path.

memory.description: Resolved guest memory in whole MiB.

boot.description: Resolved boot order: declared drive keys in order.

name.description: The blueprint's declared identity name, or null when it defaulted to the file stem.

description.description: The blueprint's human description, or null.

network.description: The resolved NIC slots keyed by slot key (D120). Each entry carries its declared attachment, the resolved interface (null when none was named), and the platform-resolved chipset.

backend-settings.description: The blueprint's per-backend settings sections, carried through verbatim.

drives.description: The resolved, enabled drives keyed by drive key. Each entry carries the drive's medium and slot plus the realized cache path (a per-machine image under disks/, an attached payload, a host directory, or null for an empty removable slot).

vm.description: The live VM identity, present only while phase is 'running' and written atomically with phase (the former standalone vm.json, folded in). The adapter verifies a session against backend-id + token before touching the VM, so a same-named VM of another home is never mistaken for this one.

variables.description: Machine variables a script `set` — the script-to-host scalar channel, read back with get-machine-var. Consumer-owned names and values (reliquary attaches no meaning to either); the rlq and reliquary key namespaces are reserved. Cleared at each start, so a variable always reports what the current boot produced, and absent until a script sets one.

driveState.description: One resolved drive. medium and slot are always present; controller is present for non-floppy drives; media names the resolved media (null in an empty removable slot, and also null for an anonymous image mounted by insert-media --file, which has no catalog identity) and materialize records how it is realized (new/difference/copy/use, null for an empty slot); size is present for a 'new' image; path is the cache location, the host path of an anonymous mounted image, or null for an empty removable slot. Beside the resolved shape sit the recorded observations, which never enter the blueprint digest: volumes and geometry for a hard disk, launch-size for a floppy.

volumes.description: How many volumes the disk actually holds, read on the host (D78) — the letter map's addressing fact. Cleared at every start, because a guest can repartition its disk and can only do so while running; absent until a stopped-machine verb reads the disk again.

launch-size.description: The byte size of the medium a floppy drive carried at launch, or null for an empty slot. The backend fixes a floppy drive's geometry from that medium, so a later live swap must match it; recorded at start, the only moment the fact is knowable.

networkState.description: One resolved NIC slot (D120). attachment and model are always present; interface is present, and null when none was named or resolved.

driveGeometry.description: What a hard disk was seen to hold, read at rest on the host (D83): read at every start (the first step, before the backend is engaged) so a running machine's describe-drives answers with this boot's starting state, refreshed by the file verbs' stopped re-reads and by an explicit refresh-drives, and read once by describe-drives for a disk never yet recorded on a down machine — read-at says when. Carries either the read facts (backing, partitioned, partitions, cylinders, volumes) or unread, the refusal in its own vocabulary and with its own id. The recognition claim is FAT12/FAT16/FAT16B over standard MBR primary/extended partitioning; everything else records as unread.

backing.description: What stands behind the device: the adapter's own format vocabulary (qemu: qcow2 or raw), or 'directory' for a directory served as one FAT volume.

partitionFacts.description: One partition-table entry as the table declares it: the type byte verbatim, and what this build reads it as.

volumeFacts.description: One volume's read facts. Geometry words are the BPB's own and null where it states none — unanswered rather than guessed; a directory-backed volume answers null throughout, its facts being the backend's to compose at attach.

vmState.description: The running VM's identity, as every backend adapter records it. backend names the adapter that owns the VM; backend-id is that backend's own machine identifier (QEMU's readable -name, shared across same-numbered machines of one blueprint; a VirtualBox machine UUID; a .vmx path; a Hyper-V VM Id); token is the per-start identifier that disambiguates them (QEMU's -uuid), required because an addressable endpoint outlives its owner; endpoint is the adapter-shaped address of the management interface (QEMU: {port}, plus vnc-port and the driving plane where the VNC control plane is served); pid is the launched process id where the backend runs as one.
